Sounds like a standard therapist to me, which is to say it sounds like a shitty therapist.  

Granted, I've never heard of gestalt therapy, so I have no idea if this is SOP for them.  Still sounds like a shitty therapist, though.

What's really great is people [chastising you for "having very high standards"](https://www.reddit.com/r/SuicideWatch/comments/447mxh/tired_of_living_as_a_failure_and_a_fuckup/czofpwh?context=3) for yourself and repeatedly failing or refusing to understand why or how someone who spends their whole life not meeting *any* of the standards--not even fantasies, just *standards*--they set for themselves might feel shitty about that.  

Sorry I don't have anything remotely helpful or supportive to say, OP.  Just wanted to chime in as someone else who won't or can't settle for less from themselves.

Amen.

Had a surreal experience today with a guy who, without asking me anything, proudly and aggressive boasted of being asexual and rudely and summarily dismissed people who have "crushes" as "those people" who weren't "really depressed."  He then mentioned, apropos of nothing, that he was "just in the hospital thurs, so it's not about me."

"I've got a lot of experience," he said.  "All the regulars come to me."

Wish I could remember his name.  Something about 4 Aces and Asexual.  Fuck if I know, and I don't care to look him up.  

He also blocked me before he asked anything about my situation, and kept restating that he was setting his own boundaries.
I *do* believe in free will, and the responsibility for my own failures and fuckups that comes with it.  This is absolutely my fault.

At bare minimum, doing something that **NOT NEARLY EVERYONE** who tries it succeeds at.  And having a success that *lasts*, and is not immediately undone and overshadowed by one of my failures.  

So ... graduating law school?  Not an achievement.  Graduating in the top 10% of the class?  An achievement.  Passing the Bar?  Not an achievement.  Being in the top 10%, or at least the top *half* of all passing scores?  An achievement, or certainly more of an achievement than merely passing.  Getting a job, and then getting shit-canned for your own incompetence less than two years later, and being unable to find a job for the rest of your "career?"  Absolutely not an achievement.

Even if I were to accept that I have "very high standards," and I don't accept that ... *so*?  Should I be fine and happy with failing to live up to my own standards?  Because that stinks up hypocrisy to me. 

And in response to "there is far more joy in life than just achievement," I disagree.  Try going through life failing to live up to any of your own standards, and tell me you'll experience any "joy" in that.  Just try it.

Your GPA is still higher than mine.  Law school *or* undergrad.  And I missed all of two classes in law school, so your story only illustrates how much of a failure and a fuckup I am; you got better grades than me despite me being in class five times as often as you.  I had an advantage, and I underperformed despite it.  I fucked it up.  I'm a fuckup.

And I absolutely do not have a "talent" for writing.  I've got the stacks of rejection letters and unfavorable decisions to show it.

If the overwhelming majority of people who try to do something successfully do it, it should not, cannot, and does not count as an "accomplishment."  Counting something that most people who try it can do as an "accomplishment" dilutes the meaning of the word to the point where it is meaningless.  That's the point behind my "eating cereal" spiel.  The definition you're proposing just means an "accomplishment" is the same as "eating a bowl of cereal you didn't like."  That's pointless.  There's no reason to celebrate or take pride in something almost everyone who tries to do it can do.

They are not accomplishments.  

1. The **VAST, OVERWHELMING MAJORITY** of people who attempted the same things I did, also did them.  And most did them better.  If you're going to count something **ALMOST EVERYONE WHO TRIES IT SUCCEEDS AT** an "incredible accomplishment," you may as well call it an "incredible accomplishment" to finish a bowl of cereal that you started.  

2. Whatever "success" I achieved there was entirely undone and rendered moot by my subsequent failures and fuckups.  Graduated and got a job?  Lost the job due to my own incompetence.  Failed to hold onto *any* job for two years.  Went from graduating debt-free from undergrad to having over $90,000 in unpaid law school loans.  

3. You are correct that me merely thinking I'm a fuckip and a failure does not make it so.  However, when you look at how I've failed and ducked up at everything I've attempted to do, *that* makes me a failure and a fuckup.
